details:
ASTERRA AI is a bilingual decision-support prototype designed to help farmers near Buraydah, Saudi Arabia, explore crop rotations under water constraints.

The app uses NASA POWER daily climate data for the Buraydah area from 2000 to 2024, including temperature, precipitation and solar radiation. It presents climate trends and estimates reference evapotranspiration, an indicator of atmospheric water demand. Farmers can also record memories of good and difficult seasons and explore them alongside the climate data.

To explore rotation options, a farmer selects a soil type, enters a water budget and adjusts priorities. The app screens and ranks possible rotations using these inputs, crop characteristics and climate indicators. It also lets users explore how changes in temperature and rainfall may affect estimated water demand.

Our approach combines environmental data with farmer experience in an English and Arabic interface. We considered water scarcity, soil health, heat, accessibility and the need to communicate uncertainty. The website was built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript and deployed on Vercel.

ASTERRA AI is intended to support discussion and exploration, not replace local expertise. NASA POWER data describes a regional grid area rather than an individual field. Crop-water values, soil adjustments and rotation scores are illustrative and have not been validated with farmers or agronomists. Results should be reviewed with local agricultural and water experts before use.
